notes: Paper derives cosmological constraints on axion parameter space (m_a, f_a) from recurrent axinovae — the explosive collapse of axion stars in minihalos formed in post-inflationary scenarios. The constraint is based on requiring that the fraction of dark matter converted to relativistic axions via axinovae does not exceed ~2.6% (from decaying dark matter bounds). Three exclusion regions are presented in Fig. 1 (green, red, blue) corresponding to different assumptions about axion star growth timescales and oscillation temperature. The blue region represents the strongest constraint after optimizing over oscillation temperature. Data points are approximate extractions from the exclusion plot boundaries; exact numerical values are not tabulated in the paper. The constraint is independent of non-gravitational couplings (photon, electron, neutron) and depends only on axion self-coupling (related to f_a) and gravity.
